correctness.rationale: The circle quartic restricted to a parabola has zero cubic term; hence every four-subset has exactly one cocircular time, and at that instant its disk contains additional sites precisely when either of its paired gaps is nonconsecutive. The fourth-point test fixes the flip direction. Delaunay local-to-global gives both fan endpoints and all generic intervals. All n>=4 follows analytically; an independent exact rational checker exhaustively verifies n=4..8.

originality.rationale: The reviewed claim is the complete explicit constant-vertical-velocity Euclidean Delaunay trajectory with all and only adjacent-pair four-sum flips, exact times and endpoint fans; classical Tamari orientation, maximum chain length and known quadratic-order kinetic behavior are excluded from novelty. Six actual semantic mathematical-record searches found no covered construction in top-ranked indexed findings, and the closest primary full-text materials do not imply the exact statement. An uninspected older specialized source remains a residual historical priority risk, so this is not a proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: The natural geometric question asks which cocircularities of a fixed convex n-gon under linear site motion actually alter its Delaunay structure. The result gives every edge change and exact time for all n, exhibits the full maximum-length Tamari path and gives an output-sensitive explicit event generator. This is useful as a canonical structurally constrained kinetic example and nontrivial bridge between empty-circle geometry and associahedral order, beyond merely restating known complexity scale.
